questions.prompt: The transfer function from state-space form is
questions.explanation: The state-space to transfer function formula is \(G(s) = C(sI - A)^{-1}B + D\). The matrix \((sI - A)^{-1}\) is the resolvent. \(D\) is the direct feedthrough. The other formulas have incorrect matrix ordering.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>state to transfer</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">C   (sI-A)^{-1}   B   +   D</text></svg>

questions.prompt: The poles of the transfer function are
questions.explanation: The poles are where \((sI - A)^{-1}\) blows up, which is where \(\det(sI - A) = 0\). These are the eigenvalues of \(A\). The diagonal entries are eigenvalues only for diagonal matrices.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>poles from eigenvalues</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="142" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="123" y1="85" x2="133" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="95" x2="133" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A state-space system has \(A = -3\), \(B = 1\), \(C = 2\), \(D = 0\). The DC gain \(G(0)\) is
questions.explanation: \(G(0) = C(0 - A)^{-1}B = 2 \times (1/3) \times 1 = 0.667\). At DC, \((sI - A)^{-1}\) becomes \(-A^{-1} = 1/3\). The pole at \(-3\) means the system is stable.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>DC gain</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="70" y2="90"/><line x1="98" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="79" y1="85" x2="89" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="95" x2="89" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.explanation: The eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix are its diagonal entries. The poles are at \(-2\) and \(-5\). The question asks for one; \(-2\) is the slower pole.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>diagonal poles</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="26" y2="90"/><line x1="54" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="35" y1="85" x2="45" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="35" y1="95" x2="45" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: If the state-space realization is minimal (controllable and observable), the transfer function poles
questions.explanation: A minimal realization has no pole-zero cancellations. The transfer function degree equals the state dimension. Non-minimal realizations may have hidden modes that cancel, giving fewer poles than eigenvalues.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>minimal realization</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="70" y2="90"/><line x1="98" y1="90" x2="114" y2="90"/><line x1="142" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="123" y1="85" x2="133" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="95" x2="133" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="85" x2="89" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="95" x2="89" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A 2x2 system has \(A = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\), \(C = [1\; 1]\), \(D = 0\). The DC gain is
questions.explanation: \(G(0) = C(-A)^{-1}B = [1\; 1] \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/4\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} = 1 + 0.25 = 1.25\). Each mode contributes to the DC gain.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>diagonal A</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">0   -4</text></svg>

questions.prompt: A first-order system has pole at \(-2\) and DC gain 3. If \(D = 0\), then \(C \cdot B / |A|\) equals
questions.explanation: DC gain is \(-CA^{-1}B = CB/|A| = 3\). With \(|A| = 2\), \(CB = 6\). The pole location is \(-2\), so \(A = -2\). Solving: \(C \cdot 1 \cdot B / 2 = 3\) gives \(CB = 6\).
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>first-order gain</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A zero of the transfer function corresponds to
questions.explanation: Zeros are where the numerator is zero, meaning \(G(s) = 0\). For SISO, this is where \(C(sI-A)^{-1}B + D = 0\). Zeros can affect the transient response shape and the high-frequency rolloff.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>pole and zero</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="48" y2="90"/><line x1="76" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><circle cx="62" cy="90" r="5"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A system has poles at \(-1\) and \(-3\). The denominator of \(G(s)\) is \(s^2 + as + b\). The value of \(a\) is
questions.explanation: The denominator is \((s+1)(s+3) = s^2 + 4s + 3\). So \(a = 4\) and \(b = 3\). The sum of the poles' magnitudes is 4; the product is 3.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>characteristic polynomial</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="70" y2="90"/><line x1="98" y1="90" x2="114" y2="90"/><line x1="142" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="123" y1="85" x2="133" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="123" y1="95" x2="133" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="85" x2="89" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="79" y1="95" x2="89" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A system with \(A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{bmatrix}\) has repeated eigenvalue at \(-2\). The denominator of \(G(s)\) is \((s+2)^n\). The value of \(n\) is
questions.explanation: The matrix has a repeated eigenvalue \(-2\) with algebraic multiplicity 2. The characteristic polynomial is \((s+2)^2\). The transfer function denominator is at most this, possibly less if there are cancellations.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>repeated pole</title><line x1="20" y1="90" x2="92" y2="90"/><line x1="120" y1="90" x2="280" y2="90"/><polygon points="280,90 273.6,92.7 273.6,87.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="150" y2="16"/><polygon points="150,16 152.7,22.4 147.3,22.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="274" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="158" y="14" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><line x1="101" y1="85" x2="111" y2="95" stroke-width="1.8"/><line x1="101" y1="95" x2="111" y2="85" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>

questions.prompt: A state transformation \(T\) changes \(A\) to \(TAT^{-1}\). The transfer function
questions.explanation: A similarity transformation does not change the transfer function. The eigenvalues (poles) are preserved. The state representation changes, but the input-output behavior is the same.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>similarity transform</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">T   A   T^{-1}</text></svg>

questions.prompt: A transfer function \(G(s) = 5/(s+4)\) has one pole. A minimal realization needs at least how many states?
questions.explanation: The transfer function order is 1 (one pole, no cancellation). A minimal realization has state dimension equal to the transfer function order. More states would introduce hidden modes.
